subject: Civil Engineering
title: Seismic Design of Bridges
description: One-minute skill: Seismic Design of Bridges.

hook.text: The 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake collapsed a section of the Bay Bridge in seconds.

buildup.text: Earthquakes shake bridges sideways, vertically, and rotationally all at once.

discovery.text: Base isolation bearings let the deck slide while the ground shakes beneath it.

twist.text: Ductile detailing lets columns bend without breaking — controlled damage saves lives.

climax.text: Japan's Akashi Kaikyo Bridge survived the 1995 Kobe earthquake undamaged.

punchline.text: Earthquake-safe bridges bend and slide — they never fight the ground.

quiz.question: How do base isolation bearings protect a bridge during an earthquake?
options: They make the bridge heavier so it resists shaking
They let the deck slide while the ground moves beneath it
They absorb all earthquake energy into the foundation

details.summary: Seismic bridge design ensures bridges survive earthquakes by allowing controlled damage in specific locations while maintaining structural stability. Engineers use ductile column detailing, seismic isolation bearings.
details.whyItMatters: Bridge collapses during earthquakes can cut off emergency access when it is most needed. Seismic design has prevented thousands of collapses since modern codes were developed after the 1971 San Fernando earthquake.
takeaways: Ductile columns are designed to bend without collapsing during earthquakes
Seismic isolation bearings reduce forces transmitted to the structure
Capacity design ensures failures occur in controlled, repairable locations

faq.question: What does capacity design mean for bridge earthquake engineering?
faq.answer: Capacity design deliberately makes columns weaker than the connections and foundations they attach to, ensuring that during an earthquake, damage concentrates in the columns where it is visible and repairable. Foundations and cap beams are designed stronger to remain undamaged.

faq.question: How do seismic isolation bearings protect bridges from earthquakes?
faq.answer: Isolation bearings are flexible pads placed between the deck and piers that decouple the deck from ground shaking. They lengthen the bridge's natural period, reducing the forces transmitted to the structure by up to 75%. Lead-rubber and friction pendulum bearings are the most common types.
